# Fast-CI inputs

The GitHub-shaped records are synthetic boundary inputs, not CI measurements. Their
40-minute reference is an illustrative shard duration; the tests also change
the baseline to prove that the gate consumes
main's evidence rather than freezing that illustrative duration. No test waits
for or claims a hosted run.

`interface.json` proposes the observer test interface: the normal
app accepts the existing observer's `joint` action through `--test-observer`
only when `EDI_TEST_OBSERVERS=1` and an active pytest context are present. The
normal/default launch and a switch without test context refuse that observer
request. Positive use changes a real loaded project's fitting mode; it is not
an existence-only receipt. The flag and front-door spelling are test interface
choices that let fixtures exercise the normal delivered app.

The time-gate CLI takes GitHub job-record documents with `--current` and `--main`,
plus the independently expected current `--run-id` and PR source `--head-sha`.
The synthetic contract binds run 111 at head c; these operands stay unchanged
when a negative control mutates the supplied record. Parser failure cannot stand
in for inspecting malformed evidence.
It compares each complete system shard with its matching main shard, refuses
incomplete or mismatched evidence, ignores unrelated jobs, and exits nonzero
with the affected shard and main comparison when its ratio exceeds 1.2. CI must
collect the actual job records and invoke that same entry point after the system
jobs. This interface permits any internal implementation and artifact format.

App-building observations move out of PR fixture execution. Native core-only
probes remain allowed. The policy witness exercises literal, aliased, wrapped,
shell, composed and helper-script build channels; the normal observer runtime
checks use the already-built app and never invoke an app build task.

The offline run documents include `expected_system_shards`, a map
from the independently declared platform to its partition count. Both documents
must prove that complete inventory, not merely agree on their received names.
The real CI producer must derive this declaration from its workflow matrix; the
synthetic documents declare it explicitly so omitted platforms can be exercised.
The comparator and this field are an operational interface proposal, not an
extra hosted measurement or a frozen three-part matrix.

The `nightly-only` group permits separately built
observers only outside PR/main shard execution. Its `paths` are exercised through
the actual selector for Linux and macOS PR, push and schedule events. The older
nightly group was not an off-PR declaration. Dependency traversal begins at the
actual PR test files and follows used imported functions and launched Python,
shell and browser helpers. Compiler queries, header-only inspections, ordinary
native probes and unexecuted build helpers remain allowed.

Runtime factory checks use a Python audit hook at actual process entry points,
including Popen, subprocess wrappers, shell and POSIX spawn. It blocks an app
build before execution; deliberately blocked negative controls are allowed
inside this proven guard. Every PR observer family must identify and execute the
normal delivered app. The separately built scan-app and thread-selector families
are instead checked through their declared nightly selection.

The workflow controls replay the actual critical shell command with offline
process transports, preserving the workflow's shell flags. Positive execution,
process refusal and numerical failure all cross the same shell boundary. The
artifact paths require PR-active producer/upload/consumer/download steps and
the real producer dependency. Mutation controls exercise disabled jobs/steps,
PR-excluding expressions, missing dependencies, command echoes, swallowed
failures, custom shell policy and continue-on-error. These are wiring proofs;
they do not substitute for the eventual hosted app/artifact and timing run.

The off-PR inventory now includes the assigned hidden compiler/host tests and
both thread-selector and scan-screen browser observers. The policy separately
checks that every reachable nightly app build is in `app_builders`; adding an
undeclared helper cannot hide a new builder behind the group exemption.

Observer timeouts enumerate descendants before terminating the launcher, stop
each discovered generation, and kill children even when they have separate
sessions. Exact binary/project argument identity also finds an observer that
was already reparented. The detached-child control exercises this cleanup rather
than relying on `killpg` to include every child of `pixi run`.

The build policy covers ordinary accident paths: shared autouse or requested pytest fixtures,
conftest setup hooks, imported module initialization, a reused helper invoking
ninja/make's edi_app target, a shell helper that first changes directory, and a
Python child that launches the compiler. These are realistic setup/helper routes;
unrelated compiler queries and native core probes remain permitted. Arbitrary
generated programs, custom plugin loaders and deliberately obfuscated commands
have no demonstrated accident path here and are recorded rather than gated.

The migrated desktop scan-screen factory has an independent normal-app reuse
witness even while its browser/scientific companion file is nightly-only. Its
real Python child launches the delivered app and completes a settings request;
the guard then stops the remaining nightly population. Module setup cost is
reported once by the canonical fixture-cost recorder and is never discarded.

Timing replay now executes the real workflow collection commands against offline
GitHub API transport and the real production comparator. Current run ID/head
111/c and main run ID/head 222/b are distinct; stale IDs, wrong heads, swapped
inputs and aliasing refuse. The synthetic PR merge SHA differs from the PR head.
The workflow must bind the actual GITHUB_RUN_ID and PR head, through context or
explicit arguments; internal implementation remains free. Both collector and
comparator steps must execute and enforce on ordinary PRs.
